args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 production deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying, and check why it was promoted even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Cause:** After the v2.3.1 deploy, the service failed health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and has paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the current state.
- **Follow-up:** The release candidate for v2.3.1 was already failing in staging but was still pushed to production. That needs looking into, along with the root cause, before v2.3.1 is deployed again. I noted both in the incident.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
